content.title: Bank of America Elevates CEO Contenders in Management Shuffle
content.summary: Bank of America  Chief Executive Officer Brian Moynihan has named two longtime executives as co-presidents and plans to expand its chief financial officer’s role in the bank’s most significant set of senior management changes in four years.  The moves spotlight three leaders viewed internally and across the banking industry as potential successors to Moynihan, 65, who has run the second-largest U.S. lender since 2010.  In a memo describing the changes on Friday, Moynihan said he plans to stay in his role through the next decade, or to 2030, reiterating guidance he has shared with employees in recent years.

content.title: Bank of America Puts Three Executives in Front of CEO Succession Race
content.summary: Bank of America  appointed two new co-presidents and elevated the title of its chief financial officer Friday, moves that identify them as the most likely potential successors for longtime Chief Executive  Brian Moynihan.  The bank tapped  Dean Athanasia,  who leads the consumer and commercial banking operations, and  Jim DeMare,  who runs the global markets division, as the co-presidents of the entire bank.  CFO  Alastair Borthwick  was given the title of executive vice president.

content.title: Bank of America Plans Shake-Up of Senior Leadership Ranks
content.description: Bank of America is planning a shake-up of its senior leadership ranks in a move that narrows the slate of leaders who could one day succeed long-time CEO Brian Moynihan. The discussion involves expanding the role of Jim DeMare, who runs the firm's trading business, along with promotions for other senior leaders, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Sridhar Natarajan has more on "Bloomberg The Close."
